description: GREATEST and LEAST order a MIXED temporal set in its WIDEST member's family: a DATE beside a TIMESTAMP is read at midnight and the answer is a timestamp, whichever side each was written on. Frostlake refused all of these - "Invalid argument types for function 'GREATEST': (DATE, TIMESTAMP_NTZ(9))" - because the value channel compared LocalDate with LocalDateTime and found no common ordering. The DATE does not always win: an earlier one loses to the timestamp, which is what shows the comparison is by INSTANT and not by family. Three arguments order the same way, two DATEs stay a DATE (the widening only happens where something wider is present) and a TIME stays OUTSIDE the order - live refuses it beside a timestamp and so does this, which is what keeps the widening honest. Values are read through TO_VARCHAR so the ENGINE renders them: read raw, the two JDBC drivers format timestamps differently and the comparison would measure the driver rather than the answer. Converted 1:1 from query/TemporalOrderingTest (now retired).
